findings: S2: 01-PRD.md lists 9 must-have features against this prompt's 3-6 bound. reference/G §G.2.1 raises the cap to 6-10 when a companion document is supplied, which is this task (prd/waze_prd.md). 9 is inside the raised band; recorded rather than silently passed.

S5: 04-uiux-brief.md carries colour as family, tone and shade and motion as named moments, not as hex values, millisecond durations or cubic-bezier curves. This prompt's S5 predates the settled number rule (generate_instruction.md §4 'The number rule, DECIDED'), which tools/source_lint.py owns and G51 enforces: a hex anywhere in the brief is a G51 failure. The exact type scale and the WCAG AA bar ARE carried, as that rule requires.

A1: '## Build plan' is absent. generate_instruction.md §2.1 makes it NOT baseline ('6/6 shipped human-authored reference briefs omit it'), so its absence is the intended state and `spec_sections_given` omits the token to match. The other ten H2s are present and canonically spelled, plus the unbudgeted '## Front-end specification' that reference/G §G.3 licenses.
B3: same cause as A1. Two of the three levers ('## Technical requirements', '## Data model') are present; '## Build plan' is withheld at baseline rather than missing by accident.

C1: nine numbered rules are presence assertions about rendered chrome (5, 6, 7, 9, 11, 13, 33, 35, 36) and carry no distinct negative case, because their negative case is the plain absence of the named element. Every behavioural rule carries an explicit negative case with a described rejection outcome.

C5: '## Data model' states the no-overlap rule as an observable invariant ('exactly one is accepted, the other is rejected... This must hold at the database level') rather than as a named index or constraint. INV9 and G43 forbid naming the storage-engine construct in that section; tools/prescription_lint.py fails the spelling this check asks for.

C7: '## Core features' is 13,664 characters, past the 2,500-character point where run_rubric.py slices it, so rules past roughly the leave-time scheduler reach the agent in full but not the judge. generate_instruction.md §4 settles that the brief has no length limit and that a past-slice section 'is information, not a finding'; judge_score never touches reward, and the criteria carry their own evaluation_rule. window_lint.py (G33) reports the same number and passes.

RC-01: judgment-class obligations are split between two channels rather than all claimed by the rubric. 24 are claimed by a criterion's items map; the remaining rendered-surface items are claimed by a browser substep instead. channel_lint.py rule (3) forbids a browser substep and a rubric criterion claiming one item, so claiming them all here would fail G28. Every judgment-class obligation is claimed exactly once across the two: coverage_map.py (G24) reports no orphan.

RC-12: R11 asserts the footer tagline, an exact copy string a pytest HTTP assertion could decide. It is retained because the judged half is the placement claim -- the tagline sits under the wordmark -- which pytest cannot decide, and because `functionality` needs a second criterion to hold its 0.25 share. No pytest test asserts that string, so the two channels do not overlap.

SCHEMA-011: the file carries four keys the prompt's canonical template does not list -- [metadata].variant_axes, [metadata].launch_surface, [metadata].design_direction and the [delivery] table. Each is required by a mechanical gate on this kit revision: validate_task.py T3 fails a b-variant without variant_axes, flag_lint.py (G41) fails a bundle without launch_surface or design_direction, and stage-4 requires [delivery] on every new bundle. The template in this prompt predates them.

SCHEMA-013: section order follows the canonical template with [delivery] inserted between [verifier] and [[artifacts]], which the template does not place because it predates the block. Same cause as SCHEMA-011.

CMP-011: the `main` service publishes `4173:4173`. CMP-022 in this same registry requires it, and validate_task.py COMPOSE_MAIN_REQUIRED fails a bundle whose `main` sets no `ports` -- the verifier reaches the app through that publish. The two rows contradict each other; the mechanically enforced one governs. No sidecar publishes a host port.

CMP-020: `main` carries `extra_hosts` and `ports` beyond `depends_on`. Both are demanded by CMP-022 and by validate_task.py: without `host.docker.internal:host-gateway` the agent's first completion fails and Harbor loses the trial. Same contradiction as CMP-011.
